message.en: Great work on your workbook, Lyra! Open Homework Review to see what you got right and what we will fix together. Then open today's workbook.
message.zh: Lyra，你的练习册做得很好！打开“作业讲评”，看看哪些做对了、哪些我们一起改。然后打开今天的练习册。

intro.en: Go through these slides with Roy. Tap 🔊 to hear each slide read aloud.
intro.zh: 和 Roy 老师一起看这些幻灯片。点 🔊 可以听朗读。

caption.en: A stadium wave: each person only stands up and sits down, but the wave travels all the way along!
caption.zh: 体育场人浪：每个人只是站起来再坐下，但“浪”一直往前走！

points.en: A wave is a disturbance that transfers ENERGY from one place to another.
points.zh: 波是一种扰动，把能量从一个地方传到另一个地方。

points.en: The wave moves along, but the stuff it travels through stays in the same place.
points.zh: 波向前走，但它经过的东西留在原地。

remember.zh: 波传递的是能量，不是物质。

points.en: In a transverse wave, the vibrations are PERPENDICULAR (at 90°) to the direction the wave travels.
points.zh: 横波的振动方向和传播方向垂直（成 90°）。

points.en: Watch the orange dot: it only goes up and down, while the wave moves sideways.
points.zh: 看橙色的点：它只是上下动，而波在横着走。

points.en: Examples: light, all electromagnetic waves, ripples on water.
points.zh: 例子：光、所有电磁波、水面的波纹。

points.en: Crest = the top. Trough = the bottom. The dashed line is the rest position.
points.zh: 波峰 = 最高点。波谷 = 最低点。虚线是平衡位置。

points.en: Amplitude = from the REST position to the crest.
points.zh: 振幅 = 从平衡位置到波峰。

points.en: Wavelength = from one crest to the next crest.
points.zh: 波长 = 从一个波峰到下一个波峰。

remember.en: Amplitude is NOT crest to trough. It is rest position to crest.
remember.zh: 振幅不是波峰到波谷，而是平衡位置到波峰。

points.en: In a longitudinal wave, the vibrations are PARALLEL to the direction the wave travels.
points.zh: 纵波的振动方向和传播方向平行。

points.en: Compression = particles squashed close together. Rarefaction = particles spread further apart.
points.zh: 密部 = 粒子挤得很近。疏部 = 粒子分得更开。

points.en: Sound is a longitudinal wave. Think of pushing and pulling a slinky.
points.zh: 声音是纵波。想一想推拉弹簧玩具。

main.zh: 频率 = 波的数量 ÷ 时间

points.en: Frequency = the number of complete waves passing a point each second.
points.zh: 频率 = 每秒通过某一点的完整波的数量。

points.en: It is measured in hertz (Hz). 1 Hz = one wave per second.
points.zh: 单位是赫兹 (Hz)。1 赫兹 = 每秒 1 个波。

items.en: Sound needs a medium: air, water or a solid.
items.zh: 声音需要介质：空气、水或固体。

items.en: Space is a vacuum: no particles, so no sound.
items.zh: 太空是真空：没有粒子，所以没有声音。

items.en: Light CAN travel through a vacuum.

points.en: Medium = a substance or material that a wave travels through.
points.zh: 介质 = 波传播时经过的物质。

points.en: Vacuum = a space containing no particles.
points.zh: 真空 = 没有任何粒子的空间。

points.en: Sound in air: about 340 m/s. In water: about 1500 m/s. Light: about 300,000 km/s!
points.zh: 声音在空气中约 340 米/秒，在水中约 1500 米/秒。光约 300,000 公里/秒！

label.en: Low pitch: few waves each second
High pitch: many waves each second

points.en: Pitch = how high or low a sound seems. It depends on FREQUENCY only.
points.zh: 音调 = 声音听起来有多高或多低，只由频率决定。

points.en: More waves squeezed in = higher frequency = higher pitch.
points.zh: 波越密 = 频率越高 = 音调越高。

points.en: Loudness (volume) = how loud or quiet a sound seems. It depends on AMPLITUDE.
points.zh: 响度 = 声音听起来有多大或多小，由振幅决定。

points.en: Taller wave = bigger amplitude = louder sound. Sound level is measured in decibels (dB).
points.zh: 波越高 = 振幅越大 = 声音越大。声音大小的单位是分贝 (dB)。

remember.en: Pitch = frequency ONLY. Loudness = amplitude ONLY.
remember.zh: 音调只看频率，响度只看振幅。

points.en: Move the amplitude slider: the wave gets taller and the sound gets louder.
points.zh: 拖动振幅滑块：波变高，声音变大。

points.en: Move the frequency slider: more waves and a higher pitch.
points.zh: 拖动频率滑块：波变多，音调变高。

items.zh: 人类能听到 20 到 20,000 赫兹

points.en: Audible range = the range of frequencies an animal can hear.
points.zh: 可听范围 = 动物能听到的频率范围。

points.en: Echo = a sound heard again after it reflects off a surface. Bats and dolphins use echolocation; ships use sonar.
points.zh: 回声 = 声音反射后再次被听到。蝙蝠和海豚用回声定位，船用声呐。

steps.en: pinna
steps.zh: 耳廓

steps.en: auditory canal
steps.zh: 外耳道

steps.en: eardrum
steps.zh: 鼓膜

steps.en: ossicles
steps.zh: 听小骨

steps.en: cochlea
steps.zh: 耳蜗

steps.en: auditory nerve
steps.zh: 听神经

steps.en: brain
steps.zh: 大脑

points.en: The pinna collects sound. The eardrum vibrates. The ossicles (3 tiny bones) make the vibrations bigger.
points.zh: 耳廓收集声音，鼓膜振动，听小骨（3 块小骨头）把振动放大。

points.en: The cochlea turns vibrations into electrical signals. The auditory nerve carries them to the brain.
points.zh: 耳蜗把振动变成电信号，听神经把信号传到大脑。

points.en: Very loud sounds can damage the tiny hair cells in the cochlea forever.
points.zh: 很大的声音会永久损伤耳蜗里的毛细胞。

points.en: Now practise with the flashcards, the fill-in-the-blanks and the quiz.
points.zh: 现在用闪卡、填空和小测来练习吧。

canNow.en: I can now explain transverse and longitudinal waves, frequency, pitch, loudness and how we hear.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释横波和纵波、频率、音调、响度，以及我们怎样听到声音。

title.en: A2 and A3 Fix-It: Element, Compound or Mixture?
title.zh: A2 和 A3 改错：元素、化合物还是混合物？

intro.en: Ask 3 questions: (1) How many kinds of particle? One = pure, two or more = mixture. (2) Are the atoms joined? (3) Same atoms = element, different atoms joined = compound.
intro.zh: 问 3 个问题：(1) 有几种粒子？一种 = 纯净物，两种或以上 = 混合物。(2) 原子结合了吗？(3) 相同原子 = 元素，不同原子结合 = 化合物。

why.en: Air is many gases (nitrogen, oxygen and more) mixed together, NOT joined.
why.zh: 空气是很多种气体混在一起，没有结合。

why.en: Two capital letters, Na and Cl, chemically joined. That is a compound.
why.zh: 两个大写字母 Na 和 Cl 结合在一起，是化合物。

why.en: Brass is an alloy: copper and zinc mixed, not joined. Alloys are mixtures.
why.zh: 黄铜是合金：铜和锌混在一起，没有结合。合金是混合物。

questions.q: Which TWO words describe nitrogen (N₂) at room temperature?

why.en: N₂ has only one kind of atom (N), so it is an element. Nitrogen is a gas in the air.
why.zh: N₂ 只有一种原子，所以是元素。氮气是空气里的气体。

why.en: One capital letter (Br), one kind of atom: element. Bromine is one of the two liquid elements.
why.zh: 只有一个大写字母 Br，一种原子：元素。溴是两种液态元素之一。

why.en: After heating, iron and sulfur are chemically joined. A magnet cannot pull the iron out. It is a compound.
why.zh: 加热后铁和硫化学结合，磁铁吸不出铁，所以是化合物。

why.en: Petrol has no single formula. It is many things mixed together: a mixture.
why.zh: 汽油没有一个化学式，是很多东西混在一起：混合物。

why.en: O₂ has one capital letter, so only one kind of atom.
why.zh: O₂ 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子。

questions.q: A box has blue-blue molecules and single red atoms, not joined to each other. What is the FULL name?

why.en: Blue-blue = an element (same atoms). Red atoms = another element. Two elements, not joined. Always write the FULL name in a test.
why.zh: 蓝蓝 = 一种元素，红原子 = 另一种元素，没有结合。考试要写完整的名称。

questions.q: A box has only blue-blue molecules. What is the FULL name?

why.en: Every particle is the same, and each one is the same atoms joined. Write "element (molecules)", not just "molecules".
why.zh: 每个粒子都一样，都是相同的原子结合。要写 element (molecules)，不能只写 molecules。

canNow.en: I can now tell an element, a compound and a mixture apart, and use the full name.
canNow.zh: 我现在能分辨元素、化合物和混合物，并写出完整名称。

title.en: M1.1 Counting Atoms: Write It Once
title.zh: M1.1 数原子：算式只写一次

intro.en: Atoms in many molecules = number of molecules × atoms in ONE molecule. Write that working once, then stop.
intro.zh: 很多分子里的原子 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。只写一次算式，然后停。

items.q: How many atoms are in 4 molecules of CO₂?

hint.en: Find the atoms in ONE molecule first. Then multiply by the number of molecules. Write the working only ONCE.
hint.zh: 先算一个分子里有几个原子，再乘分子的个数。算式只写一次。

steps.en: One CO₂ has 1 C + 2 O.
steps.zh: 一个 CO₂ 有 1 个 C 和 2 个 O。

steps.en: Multiply by the number of molecules. Stop here: do not multiply again!
steps.zh: 乘以分子的个数。到这里就停：不要再乘一次！

why.en: Total = number of molecules × atoms in one molecule.
why.zh: 总数 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。

items.q: How many HYDROGEN atoms are in 5 molecules of CH₄?

hint.en: Find the atoms in ONE molecule first. Then multiply by the number of molecules. Write the working only ONCE.
hint.zh: 先算一个分子里有几个原子，再乘分子的个数。算式只写一次。

steps.en: One CH₄ has 4 hydrogen atoms. (We only count H.)
steps.zh: 一个 CH₄ 有 4 个氢原子（只数 H）。

steps.en: Multiply by the number of molecules. Stop here: do not multiply again!
steps.zh: 乘以分子的个数。到这里就停：不要再乘一次！

why.en: Total = number of molecules × atoms in one molecule.
why.zh: 总数 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。

items.q: How many atoms are in 3 molecules of H₂O?

hint.en: Find the atoms in ONE molecule first. Then multiply by the number of molecules. Write the working only ONCE.
hint.zh: 先算一个分子里有几个原子，再乘分子的个数。算式只写一次。

steps.en: One H₂O has 2 H + 1 O.
steps.zh: 一个 H₂O 有 2 个 H 和 1 个 O。

steps.en: Multiply by the number of molecules. Stop here: do not multiply again!
steps.zh: 乘以分子的个数。到这里就停：不要再乘一次！

why.en: Total = number of molecules × atoms in one molecule.
why.zh: 总数 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。

items.q: How many atoms are in 2 molecules of H₂SO₄?

hint.en: Find the atoms in ONE molecule first. Then multiply by the number of molecules. Write the working only ONCE.
hint.zh: 先算一个分子里有几个原子，再乘分子的个数。算式只写一次。

steps.en: One H₂SO₄ has 2 H + 1 S + 4 O.
steps.zh: 一个 H₂SO₄ 有 2 个 H、1 个 S 和 4 个 O。

steps.en: Multiply by the number of molecules. Stop here: do not multiply again!
steps.zh: 乘以分子的个数。到这里就停：不要再乘一次！

why.en: Total = number of molecules × atoms in one molecule.
why.zh: 总数 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。

items.q: How many OXYGEN atoms are in 3 molecules of CO₂?

hint.en: Find the atoms in ONE molecule first. Then multiply by the number of molecules. Write the working only ONCE.
hint.zh: 先算一个分子里有几个原子，再乘分子的个数。算式只写一次。

steps.en: One CO₂ has 2 oxygen atoms. (We only count O.)
steps.zh: 一个 CO₂ 有 2 个氧原子（只数 O）。

steps.en: Multiply by the number of molecules. Stop here: do not multiply again!
steps.zh: 乘以分子的个数。到这里就停：不要再乘一次！

why.en: Total = number of molecules × atoms in one molecule.
why.zh: 总数 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。

items.q: How many atoms are in 2 molecules of C₃H₈?

hint.en: Find the atoms in ONE molecule first. Then multiply by the number of molecules. Write the working only ONCE.
hint.zh: 先算一个分子里有几个原子，再乘分子的个数。算式只写一次。

steps.en: One C₃H₈ has 3 C + 8 H.
steps.zh: 一个 C₃H₈ 有 3 个 C 和 8 个 H。

steps.en: Multiply by the number of molecules. Stop here: do not multiply again!
steps.zh: 乘以分子的个数。到这里就停：不要再乘一次！

why.en: Total = number of molecules × atoms in one molecule.
why.zh: 总数 = 分子个数 × 一个分子里的原子数。

canNow.en: I can now count the atoms in many molecules with one multiplication.
canNow.zh: 我现在能用一次乘法数出很多分子里的原子。

title.en: A5 to A7 Fix-It: Reactions, Changes and States
title.zh: A5 到 A7 改错：反应、变化和物态

intro.en: Naming rule: keep the metal name, change the non-metal ending: oxygen → oxide, chlorine → chloride, sulfur → sulfide. 2 oxygens = dioxide.
intro.zh: 命名规则：金属名字不变，非金属结尾改成 -ide：oxygen → oxide，chlorine → chloride，sulfur → sulfide。2 个氧 = dioxide。

questions.q: Which reaction is: compound → two elements?
options: carbon dioxide + calcium hydroxide → calcium carbonate + water

why.en: Water is ONE compound. It splits into TWO elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
why.zh: 水是一种化合物，分解成两种元素：氢和氧。

questions.q: Which reaction is: element + element → compound?
options: calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide

why.en: Zinc and sulfur are both elements. They join to make one compound, zinc sulfide.
why.zh: 锌和硫都是元素，结合成一种化合物：硫化锌。

questions.q: Zinc is heated with sulfur. Name the solid that forms.

why.en: Keep the metal name (zinc). Change sulfur to sulfide.
why.zh: 金属名字不变（zinc），sulfur 改成 sulfide。

why.en: SO₂ has 2 oxygen atoms. 2 = di, so it is sulfur DIoxide.
why.zh: SO₂ 有 2 个氧原子，2 = di，所以是 sulfur dioxide。

why.en: A new substance forms and you cannot uncook the egg. That is a chemical change.
why.zh: 生成了新物质，鸡蛋煮熟后变不回去，是化学变化。

why.en: Gas turns back into liquid: condensing. (Think of water drops on a cold glass.)
why.zh: 气体变回液体叫凝结（像冷杯子外面的小水珠）。

options: There are 2 liquid elements at room temperature.

why.en: Mercury and bromine are the 2 liquid elements. Most elements are metals, most metals are NOT magnetic, and there are about 118 elements.
why.zh: 汞和溴是两种液态元素。大部分元素是金属，大部分金属没有磁性，元素大约有 118 种。

questions.q: Which TWO elements are liquids at 1000 °C?

why.en: Liquid = hotter than the melting point but colder than the boiling point. Aluminium: 660 to 2520. Magnesium: 650 to 1100. 1000 is inside both.
why.zh: 液体 = 比熔点高、比沸点低。铝：660 到 2520。镁：650 到 1100。1000 在两个范围里面。

questions.context: Melting point / boiling point (°C): aluminium 660 / 2520, iron 1540 / 2760, magnesium 650 / 1100, mercury -39 / 357

why.en: Negative numbers are smaller than 0. The bigger the number after the minus sign, the SMALLER it is: -100 < -39 < -5 < 0 < 12.
why.zh: 负数比 0 小。负号后面的数越大，这个数越小：-100 < -39 < -5 < 0 < 12。

questions.q: What does a magnet show about the iron + sulfur MIXTURE and iron SULFIDE?
options: It pulls iron out of both.
It pulls iron out of the mixture, but not out of iron sulfide.
It cannot pull iron out of either.

why.en: In the mixture the iron is not joined, so the magnet pulls it out. In iron sulfide the iron is joined to sulfur, so it is a new substance.
why.zh: 混合物里的铁没有结合，磁铁能吸出来。硫化铁里的铁和硫结合了，是新物质，吸不出来。

canNow.en: I can now name compounds, spot chemical changes and use melting and boiling points.
canNow.zh: 我现在能给化合物命名、认出化学变化，并会用熔点和沸点。

title.en: M1.2 Negative Numbers, Temperature and Mass

intro.en: A number line helps: count up to 0, then count on from 0. Mass change = mass after - mass before.
intro.zh: 数轴能帮你：先数到 0，再从 0 往后数。质量变化 = 反应后 - 反应前。

items.q: The temperature goes from -5 °C to 8 °C. How many degrees did it go up?

hint.en: Draw a number line or a thermometer. Count the gap.
hint.zh: 画一条数轴或温度计，数一数中间的距离。

steps.en: From -5 up to 0 is 5 degrees.
steps.zh: 从 -5 升到 0 是 5 度。

steps.en: From 0 up to 8 is 8 degrees. Add the two parts.
steps.zh: 从 0 升到 8 是 8 度。把两段加起来。

why.en: Count the jump to 0, then the jump from 0. Same as 8 - (-5) = 8 + 5.
why.zh: 先数到 0，再从 0 往上数。和 8 - (-5) = 8 + 5 一样。

items.q: Mercury melts at -39 °C and boils at 357 °C. How many degrees are between them?

hint.en: Draw a number line or a thermometer. Count the gap.
hint.zh: 画一条数轴或温度计，数一数中间的距离。

steps.en: From -39 up to 0 is 39 degrees.
From 0 up to 357 is 357 degrees. Add them. (Subtracting a negative = adding.)
steps.zh: 从 0 到 357 是 357 度，加起来。（减负数 = 加正数）

why.en: 357 - (-39) is the same as 357 + 39.

items.q: Iron filings weighed 2.0 g. After the reaction, the iron sulfide weighed 2.8 g. How much did the mass increase?

hint.en: Draw a number line or a thermometer. Count the gap.
hint.zh: 画一条数轴或温度计，数一数中间的距离。

steps.en: Mass increase = mass after - mass before.
steps.zh: 增加的质量 = 反应后 - 反应前。

why.en: The mass went up because 0.8 g of sulfur joined the iron. Atoms are never lost or made.
why.zh: 质量增加是因为 0.8 克硫和铁结合了。原子不会消失，也不会凭空出现。

items.q: 5.0 g of magnesium is heated in air. It makes 8.3 g of magnesium oxide. How much oxygen joined the magnesium?

hint.en: Draw a number line or a thermometer. Count the gap.
hint.zh: 画一条数轴或温度计，数一数中间的距离。

steps.en: Oxygen that joined = mass after - mass before.
steps.zh: 结合的氧 = 反应后 - 反应前。

why.en: Oxygen from the air joined the magnesium, so the mass went up by 3.3 g.
why.zh: 空气里的氧和镁结合了，所以质量增加了 3.3 克。

canNow.en: I can now find temperature gaps with negative numbers and work out mass changes.
canNow.zh: 我现在能用负数算温差，也能算出质量变化。

intro.en: These are your school's keyword definitions. Say each word out loud, then flip the card.
intro.zh: 这些是学校关键词表里的定义。大声读出单词，再翻卡片。

cards.back: A disturbance that transfers energy from one place to another.
cards.zhBack: 把能量从一个地方传到另一个地方的扰动。

cards.back: A wave in which vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of travel.
cards.zhBack: 振动方向和传播方向垂直的波。

cards.back: A wave in which vibrations are parallel to the direction of travel.
cards.zhBack: 振动方向和传播方向平行的波。

cards.back: The maximum distance a point on a wave moves from its resting position.
cards.zhBack: 波上一点离开平衡位置的最大距离。

cards.back: The distance between two corresponding points on consecutive waves, such as crest to crest.
cards.zhBack: 相邻两个波上对应点之间的距离，比如波峰到波峰。

cards.back: The number of complete waves passing a point each second.
cards.zhBack: 每秒通过某一点的完整波的数量。

cards.back: The unit used to measure frequency. One hertz equals one wave per second.
cards.zhBack: 频率的单位。1 赫兹 = 每秒 1 个波。

cards.back: A substance or material through which a wave travels.
cards.zhBack: 波传播时经过的物质。

cards.back: A repeated movement backwards and forwards around a resting position.
cards.zhBack: 在平衡位置附近来回重复的运动。

cards.back: A space containing no particles.
cards.zhBack: 没有任何粒子的空间。

cards.back: A region of a longitudinal wave where particles are close together.
cards.zhBack: 纵波中粒子靠得很近的区域。

cards.back: A region of a longitudinal wave where particles are spread further apart.
cards.zhBack: 纵波中粒子分得更开的区域。

canNow.en: I can now explain the 12 key words for waves.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释 12 个关于波的关键词。

intro.en: Tap a word, then tap its meaning. Take your time.
intro.zh: 先点一个词，再点它的意思。慢慢来。

pairs.b: moves energy from place to place
moving back and forth again and again

canNow.en: I can now match the wave words to their meanings.
canNow.zh: 我现在能把波的词汇和意思配对。

title.en: B2 and B3 Sound and Hearing: Key Words
title.zh: B2 和 B3 声音和听觉：关键词

intro.en: Sound words first, then the ear from outside to inside: pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, ossicles, cochlea, auditory nerve.
intro.zh: 先学声音的词，再学耳朵从外到内：耳廓、外耳道、鼓膜、听小骨、耳蜗、听神经。

cards.back: How high or low a sound seems. It depends on the frequency of the sound wave.
cards.zhBack: 声音听起来有多高或多低，由频率决定。

cards.back: How loud or quiet a sound seems. It is related to the amplitude and intensity of the sound wave.
cards.zhBack: 声音听起来有多大或多小，和振幅有关。

cards.back: The unit used to measure sound level. The decibel scale is logarithmic.
cards.zhBack: 测量声音大小的单位。

cards.back: The range of sound frequencies that an animal can hear. For humans, this is approximately 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
cards.zhBack: 能听到的声音频率范围，人类大约是 20 到 20,000 赫兹。

cards.back: Sound with a frequency higher than 20,000 Hz, above the usual human hearing range.
cards.zhBack: 频率高于 20,000 赫兹的声音。

cards.back: Sound with a frequency lower than 20 Hz, below the usual human hearing range.
cards.zhBack: 频率低于 20 赫兹的声音。

cards.back: A sound heard again after it has reflected off a surface.
cards.zhBack: 声音碰到表面反射回来后，又被听到。

cards.back: The use of reflected sound waves to detect objects and determine their position or distance.
cards.zhBack: 用反射回来的声波找到物体，判断位置或距离。

cards.back: A system that uses reflected sound waves to detect objects and measure distances, commonly underwater.
cards.zhBack: 用反射声波探测物体、测量距离的系统，常用在水下。

cards.back: The visible outer part of the ear that collects sound waves.
cards.zhBack: 耳朵外面看得到的部分，收集声波。

cards.back: The tube that carries sound waves from the pinna to the eardrum.
cards.zhBack: 把声波从耳廓传到鼓膜的管道。

cards.back: A thin membrane that vibrates when sound waves reach it.
cards.zhBack: 声波到达时会振动的一层薄膜。

cards.back: Three tiny bones in the middle ear that transmit and amplify vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.
cards.zhBack: 中耳里的三块小骨头，把振动传到内耳并放大。

cards.back: A spiral-shaped structure in the inner ear that converts vibrations into electrical signals.
cards.zhBack: 内耳里螺旋形的结构，把振动变成电信号。

cards.back: The nerve that carries electrical signals from the cochlea to the brain.
cards.zhBack: 把电信号从耳蜗传到大脑的神经。

canNow.en: I can now explain the key words for sound and the parts of the ear.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释声音的关键词和耳朵的各个部分。

title.en: B1 to B3 Quiz: Waves and Sound
title.zh: B1 到 B3 小测：波和声音

intro.en: The big rule: pitch = frequency ONLY, loudness = amplitude ONLY.
intro.zh: 最重要的规则：音调只看频率，响度只看振幅。

questions.q: Which kind of wave is SOUND?

why.en: In sound, particles vibrate backwards and forwards in the SAME direction the wave travels: longitudinal.
why.zh: 声音里粒子来回振动的方向和波传播方向相同：纵波。

why.en: Pitch = frequency ONLY. More waves each second = higher pitch.
why.zh: 音调只看频率。每秒波越多，音调越高。

why.en: Loudness = amplitude ONLY. Taller wave = louder sound.
why.zh: 响度只看振幅。波越高，声音越大。

questions.q: 50 waves pass a point in 2 seconds. What is the frequency?

why.en: Frequency = number of waves ÷ time = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 Hz.
why.zh: 频率 = 波的数量 ÷ 时间 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 赫兹。

questions.q: Why can sound NOT travel through space?
options: Space is a vacuum with no particles.

why.en: Sound needs a medium (particles) to vibrate. A vacuum has no particles.
why.zh: 声音需要介质（粒子）来振动。真空里没有粒子。

why.en: The human audible range is about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
why.zh: 人类的可听范围大约是 20 到 20,000 赫兹。

questions.q: Sound with a frequency HIGHER than 20,000 Hz is called...

why.en: Ultra = beyond. Ultrasound is above human hearing. Infrasound is below 20 Hz.
why.zh: ultra = 超过。超声波高于人类听力范围，次声波低于 20 赫兹。

questions.q: Which order is correct for sound going into the ear?
options: pinna → auditory canal → eardrum → ossicles → cochlea
eardrum → pinna → cochlea → ossicles → auditory canal
cochlea → ossicles → eardrum → auditory canal → pinna
pinna → eardrum → auditory canal → cochlea → ossicles

why.en: Outside to inside: pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, ossicles, cochlea, then the auditory nerve to the brain.
why.zh: 从外到内：耳廓、外耳道、鼓膜、听小骨、耳蜗，再由听神经传到大脑。

options: the rest position to the crest

why.en: Amplitude = the biggest distance from the resting position. Crest to crest is the wavelength.
why.zh: 振幅 = 离开平衡位置的最大距离。波峰到波峰是波长。

questions.q: You see lightning BEFORE you hear thunder because...
options: light travels much faster than sound

why.en: Light travels about 300,000 km every second. Sound in air is only about 340 m every second.
why.zh: 光每秒大约走 300,000 公里，空气中的声音每秒只走大约 340 米。

canNow.en: I can now explain pitch, loudness, frequency and how we hear.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释音调、响度、频率，以及我们怎样听到声音。

title.en: Fill in the Blanks: Waves and Sound

intro.en: Read the sentence, then tap the missing word.
intro.zh: 读句子，然后点出缺少的词。

items.text: A wave transfers ___ from one place to another.

why.en: Waves move energy, not matter.
why.zh: 波传递能量，不传递物质。

items.text: In a transverse wave, the vibrations are ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Transverse = at 90° to the direction of travel.
why.zh: 横波 = 和传播方向成 90°。

items.text: In a longitudinal wave, the vibrations are ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Longitudinal = same direction as the wave travels, like sound.
why.zh: 纵波 = 和传播方向相同，比如声音。

items.text: The ___ is the distance from the rest position to the top of a crest.

why.en: Amplitude: rest position to crest, not crest to trough.
why.zh: 振幅：平衡位置到波峰，不是波峰到波谷。

items.text: The distance from one crest to the next crest is the ___.

why.en: Wavelength: crest to crest.
why.zh: 波长：波峰到波峰。

items.text: The number of complete waves passing a point each second is the ___.

why.en: Frequency = waves per second.
why.zh: 频率 = 每秒的波数。

why.en: 1 hertz = 1 wave per second.
why.zh: 1 赫兹 = 每秒 1 个波。

items.text: Sound cannot travel through a ___ because there are no particles.

why.en: Sound needs particles to vibrate. A vacuum has none.
why.zh: 声音需要粒子振动，真空里没有粒子。

items.text: The ___ of a sound depends on its frequency.

why.en: Pitch = frequency ONLY.
why.zh: 音调只看频率。

items.text: The ___ is a thin membrane that vibrates when sound waves reach it.

why.en: Sound makes the eardrum vibrate, then the ossicles pass it on.
why.zh: 声音让鼓膜振动，然后听小骨把振动传下去。

canNow.en: I can now use the key words for waves and sound in sentences.
canNow.zh: 我现在能在句子里用波和声音的关键词。

title.en: Day 1: Elements, Compounds, Particles and Counting Atoms
title.zh: 第 1 天：元素、化合物、粒子图和数原子

message.en: Your atom-counting table was PERFECT. Today: full names for particle pictures, and write the multiplication only once.
message.zh: 你的数原子表格全对！今天练习：粒子图要写完整名称，乘法只写一次。

title.zh: 第 2 页：元素、化合物还是混合物？

items.q: Oxygen (O₂): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: One capital letter, so one kind of atom: element.
why.zh: 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子：元素。

items.q: Carbon dioxide (CO₂): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Two capital letters (C and O) chemically joined in one formula: compound.
why.zh: 两个大写字母 C 和 O 结合在一个化学式里：化合物。

items.q: Air: element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Air is many gases (nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide...) mixed together, not joined.
why.zh: 空气是很多种气体（氮气、氧气、二氧化碳……）混在一起，没有结合。

whyWrong.en: This one was left empty. Air has no formula, so look at the Quick check: many things mixed = mixture.
whyWrong.zh: 这题没有写。空气没有化学式，看快速判断：很多东西混在一起 = 混合物。

items.q: Magnesium (Mg): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: One capital letter, so one kind of atom: element.
why.zh: 只有一个大写字母，只有一种原子：元素。

items.q: Sodium chloride (NaCl): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Sodium and chlorine are chemically joined. That is salt, a compound.
why.zh: 钠和氯化学结合在一起，就是盐，是化合物。

whyWrong.en: NaCl has TWO capital letters (Na and Cl), so it has two kinds of atom. An element has only one.
whyWrong.zh: NaCl 有两个大写字母（Na 和 Cl），所以有两种原子。元素只有一种。

items.q: Brass: element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Brass is an alloy: copper and zinc melted and mixed, not chemically joined. Alloys are mixtures.
why.zh: 黄铜是合金：铜和锌熔化后混在一起，没有化学结合。合金是混合物。

whyWrong.en: Brass has no single formula. The metals are mixed, not joined, so it cannot be a compound.
whyWrong.zh: 黄铜没有一个化学式。金属只是混合，没有结合，所以不是化合物。

items.q: Carbon monoxide (CO): element, compound or mixture?

why.en: C and O are two capital letters: two kinds of atom joined. (Co with a small o would be cobalt, an element.)
why.zh: C 和 O 是两个大写字母：两种原子结合。（小写 o 的 Co 是钴，是元素。）

items.q: Petrol: element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Petrol has no single formula. It is many substances mixed together.
why.zh: 汽油没有一个化学式，是很多物质混在一起。

items.q: Which of these is a compound? a) carbon monoxide b) magnesium c) bromine d) brass

why.en: CO = two kinds of atom joined. Magnesium and bromine are elements; brass is a mixture.
why.zh: CO = 两种原子结合。镁和溴是元素，黄铜是混合物。

items.q: Which of these is an element? a) MgS b) NaCl c) CoO d) O₂

why.en: O₂ has one capital letter. MgS, NaCl and CoO each have two kinds of atom.
why.zh: O₂ 只有一个大写字母。MgS、NaCl 和 CoO 都有两种原子。

items.q: Which order matches: hydrogen, petrol, water?

why.en: Hydrogen = element, petrol = mixture, water (H₂O) = compound.
why.zh: 氢 = 元素，汽油 = 混合物，水 (H₂O) = 化合物。

items.q: Fill the gaps: Atoms are the smallest parts of ___. Same atoms join: a ___ is formed. Different atoms join: they form ___.

why.en: Great that you corrected "element" to "molecule" yourself! Atoms joined together make a molecule.
why.zh: 你自己把 element 改成了 molecule，太棒了！原子结合在一起就是分子。

items.q: Draw 2 atoms of the SAME colour joined. Element or compound?

why.en: Same colour = same kind of atom, so it is an element (a molecule of an element, like O₂).
why.zh: 颜色相同 = 同一种原子，所以是元素（元素的分子，比如 O₂）。

items.q: Draw 2 atoms of DIFFERENT colours joined. Element or compound?

why.en: Different colours joined = different atoms chemically joined = compound.
why.zh: 不同颜色结合 = 不同原子化学结合 = 化合物。

items.q: Box A: red-blue pairs and single blue atoms. Name the box.
items.right: mixture of an element and a compound

why.en: Red-blue pairs = different atoms joined = compound. Single blue atoms = element. Together: a mixture of an element and a compound.
why.zh: 红蓝一对 = 不同原子结合 = 化合物。单个蓝原子 = 元素。合起来：元素和化合物的混合物。

whyWrong.en: Tests ask for the FULL name. "Mixture" is true, but you must say WHAT is mixed.
whyWrong.zh: 考试要写完整名称。写 mixture 没错，但要说明是什么混在一起。

items.q: Box B: only blue-blue pairs. Name the box.

why.en: Every particle is the same: two blue atoms joined. Same atoms = element; joined = molecules.
why.zh: 每个粒子都一样：两个蓝原子结合。相同原子 = 元素；结合 = 分子。

whyWrong.en: "Molecules" is only half the name. Is it a molecule of an element or of a compound? Same colours, so: element (molecules).
whyWrong.zh: molecules 只说了一半。是元素的分子还是化合物的分子？颜色相同，所以是 element (molecules)。

items.q: Box C: blue-blue pairs and single red atoms. Name the box.

why.en: Blue-blue = an element. Single red atoms = another element. Not joined to each other: a mixture of two elements.
why.zh: 蓝蓝 = 一种元素，单个红原子 = 另一种元素，彼此没有结合：两种元素的混合物。

whyWrong.en: Tests ask for the FULL name. "Mixture" is true, but you must say WHAT is mixed.
whyWrong.zh: 考试要写完整名称。写 mixture 没错，但要说明是什么混在一起。

items.q: Box D: single yellow atoms only. Name the box.

why.en: One kind of atom, not joined: an element made of single atoms.
why.zh: 只有一种原子，没有结合：由单个原子组成的元素。

items.q: Box E: all particles are the same 3-atom molecule (yellow-red-yellow). Name the box.

why.en: All particles the same (pure), and each has different atoms joined: compound.
why.zh: 所有粒子都一样（纯净物），每个粒子里不同原子结合：化合物。

items.q: Box F: yellow-red-yellow molecules and blue-blue pairs. Name the box.
items.right: mixture of an element and a compound

why.en: Yellow-red-yellow = compound. Blue-blue = same atoms = element. So: a mixture of an element and a compound.
why.zh: 黄红黄 = 化合物。蓝蓝 = 相同原子 = 元素。所以是元素和化合物的混合物。

whyWrong.en: The blue-blue pairs are NOT a compound. Both atoms are blue (the same), so they are an element.
whyWrong.zh: 蓝蓝一对不是化合物。两个原子都是蓝色（相同），所以是元素。

items.q: Draw a mixture of two elements.
items.her: single red atoms and blue-blue pairs, not touching
items.right: two kinds of element particle, not joined to each other

why.en: Red atoms are one element, blue pairs are another, and they are not joined. Perfect.
why.zh: 红原子是一种元素，蓝色一对是另一种元素，没有结合。很好。

items.q: Draw THREE water molecules (H₂O).
items.right: three molecules, each one O joined to two H

why.en: H₂O = 1 oxygen + 2 hydrogen joined. Three molecules = three of these groups (9 atoms).
why.zh: H₂O = 1 个氧 + 2 个氢结合。三个分子 = 三组（一共 9 个原子）。

whyWrong.en: Only one molecule was drawn. Read the number in the question: THREE.
whyWrong.zh: 只画了一个分子。看题目里的数字：三个。

items.q: Draw a mixture of an element and a compound.
items.right: some same-colour pairs (element) AND some different-colour pairs (compound)

why.en: You need both kinds: same-colour particles for the element and different-colour joined particles for the compound.
why.zh: 两种都要有：颜色相同的粒子是元素，颜色不同结合的粒子是化合物。

items.q: Red and blue atoms in a box, NOT touching. Mixture or compound?

why.en: Not touching = not joined = mixture.
why.zh: 没有碰在一起 = 没有结合 = 混合物。

items.q: CO₂: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: H₂O₂: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: NaCl: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: NH₃: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: H₂SO₄: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: C₆H₁₂O₆: how many elements, atoms of each, total atoms?

why.en: Each capital letter is a new element; the small number after a symbol tells how many of that atom.
why.zh: 每个大写字母是一种新元素；符号后面的小数字表示这种原子有几个。

items.q: How many atoms in 4 molecules of CO₂?

why.en: One CO₂ has 3 atoms. 4 molecules × 3 atoms = 12 atoms.
why.zh: 一个 CO₂ 有 3 个原子。4 个分子 × 3 = 12 个原子。

whyWrong.en: 12 was already the answer (4 × 3). Multiplying by 3 again counted every atom twice. Write the working ONCE.
whyWrong.zh: 12 已经是答案了（4 × 3）。再乘 3 就把原子数了两遍。算式只写一次。

items.q: How many HYDROGEN atoms in 5 molecules of CH₄?

why.en: One CH₄ has 4 hydrogen atoms. 5 × 4 = 20.
why.zh: 一个 CH₄ 有 4 个氢原子。5 × 4 = 20。

whyWrong.en: You found 20, which is right! Then it was multiplied by 3 again. Stop when you have the total.
whyWrong.zh: 你算出了 20，是对的！但又乘了 3。算出总数就停下。

items.q: A molecule has 1 carbon atom and 4 hydrogen atoms. Write its formula.

why.en: C for carbon, H for hydrogen, small 4 after H.
why.zh: C 是碳，H 是氢，H 后面写小的 4。

items.q: Hydrogen peroxide picture (O-O in the middle, H at each end). Formula?

why.en: 2 hydrogen + 2 oxygen atoms = H₂O₂.
why.zh: 2 个氢 + 2 个氧 = H₂O₂。

items.q: Cryolite puzzle: Al = 1, Na = 3 × Al, F = 2 × Na. Formula?

why.en: Na = 3 × 1 = 3. F = 2 × 3 = 6. So Na₃AlF₆. Great detective work!
why.zh: Na = 3 × 1 = 3，F = 2 × 3 = 6，所以是 Na₃AlF₆。侦探做得好！

title.en: Day 2: Word Equations, Iron and Sulfur, Negative Numbers
title.zh: 第 2 天：文字方程式、铁和硫、负数

message.en: Word equations 1 to 6 all right, and every negative-number sum right! Today: dioxide, reaction types, and writing "because" answers.
message.zh: 文字方程式 1 到 6 全对，负数计算也全对！今天练习：dioxide、反应类型，以及用 because 写解释。

title.zh: 第 5 页：化学反应和文字方程式

items.q: lead + ___ → lead sulfide

why.en: Sulfide comes from sulfur. On the LEFT side, use the element name (no -ide).
why.zh: sulfide 来自 sulfur。左边写元素的名字（不加 -ide）。

items.q: copper + chlorine → ___

why.en: Chlorine → chloride. Small spelling tip: chloride has one L after the H: c-h-l-o-r-i-d-e.
why.zh: chlorine → chloride。拼写小提示：c-h-l-o-r-i-d-e。

items.q: zinc + sulfur → ___

why.en: Keep the metal name; the non-metal changes its ending to -ide.
why.zh: 金属名字不变；非金属结尾改成 -ide。

items.q: iron + oxygen → ___

why.en: Oxygen → oxide.
why.zh: oxygen → oxide。

items.q: ___ + oxygen → magnesium oxide

why.en: The metal name stays the same on both sides.
why.zh: 金属名字两边一样。

items.q: sodium + ___ → sodium chloride

why.en: Chloride comes from chlorine. Spelling tip: c-h-l-o-r-i-n-e (don't forget the L).
why.zh: chloride 来自 chlorine。拼写：c-h-l-o-r-i-n-e（别忘了 L）。

items.q: Challenge: sulfur + oxygen → ___ (the product is SO₂)

why.en: SO₂ has TWO oxygen atoms. Two = di, so: sulfur dioxide.
why.zh: SO₂ 有两个氧原子。二 = di，所以是 sulfur dioxide。

whyWrong.en: Oxide is the right ending, but the 2 in SO₂ must show in the name: di-oxide.
whyWrong.zh: oxide 结尾是对的，但 SO₂ 里的 2 要写进名字：di-oxide。

items.q: Which reaction is: compound → two elements?
items.her: b) carbon dioxide + calcium hydroxide → calcium carbonate + water

why.en: Water is ONE compound. It splits into TWO elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
why.zh: 水是一种化合物，分解成两种元素：氢和氧。

whyWrong.en: In b) there are two compounds on the left and two compounds on the right. No elements at all.
whyWrong.zh: b) 左边是两种化合物，右边也是两种化合物，根本没有元素。

items.q: Which reaction is: element + element → compound?

why.en: Zinc and sulfur are both elements, and they join to make one compound.
why.zh: 锌和硫都是元素，结合成一种化合物。

whyWrong.en: This one was left empty. Look for two single element names on the left.
whyWrong.zh: 这题没有写。找左边是两个元素名字的反应。

items.q: BEFORE (2 H₂ and 1 O₂) is a mixture of two ___.

why.en: H₂ and O₂ are both elements, just mixed.
why.zh: H₂ 和 O₂ 都是元素，只是混在一起。

items.q: AFTER (2 H₂O) is a ___.

why.en: Water has H and O joined: a compound. Atoms before = 6, atoms after = 6. Atoms are never lost!
why.zh: 水里 H 和 O 结合：化合物。反应前 6 个原子，反应后也是 6 个。原子不会消失！

whyWrong.en: After the reaction, the H and O atoms are joined together. Different atoms joined can't be an element.
whyWrong.zh: 反应后 H 和 O 原子结合在一起。不同原子结合不可能是元素。

title.en: Page 6: The Iron and Sulfur Story
title.zh: 第 6 页：铁和硫的故事

items.q: Give ONE way you can tell a chemical reaction took place.
items.right: e.g. it glowed brightly / a black solid formed / the colour changed

why.en: Signs of a reaction: light or heat given out, colour change, a gas, or a new substance with new properties.
why.zh: 化学反应的迹象：发光或放热、颜色改变、产生气体、或生成有新性质的新物质。

whyWrong.en: Left empty. The story says the mixture "glowed very brightly". That is one sign!
whyWrong.zh: 没有写。故事里说混合物“发出很亮的光”，这就是一个迹象！

items.q: Iron: metallic element, non-metallic element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Iron is a metal and only one kind of atom (Fe).
why.zh: 铁是金属，只有一种原子 (Fe)。

items.q: Sulfur: metallic element, non-metallic element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Sulfur is a yellow non-metal, one kind of atom (S).
why.zh: 硫是黄色的非金属，只有一种原子 (S)。

items.q: Iron sulfide: metallic element, non-metallic element, compound or mixture?

why.en: Iron and sulfur chemically joined after heating.
why.zh: 加热后铁和硫化学结合。

items.q: Iron + sulfur before heating: ?

why.en: Before heating they are just mixed. A magnet can still pull the iron out.
why.zh: 加热前只是混在一起，磁铁还能把铁吸出来。

items.q: Is iron magnetic?

why.en: Iron is one of the few magnetic metals.
why.zh: 铁是少数有磁性的金属之一。

items.q: Is sulfur magnetic?

why.en: Sulfur is a non-metal and not magnetic.
why.zh: 硫是非金属，没有磁性。

items.q: Is iron sulfide magnetic?

why.en: Iron sulfide is a NEW substance with new properties. It is not magnetic.
why.zh: 硫化铁是新物质，有新的性质，没有磁性。

items.q: Zinc is heated with sulfur. Name the solid that forms.

why.en: Keep the metal name (zinc) + sulfur becomes sulfide: zinc sulfide.
why.zh: 金属名字不变（zinc）+ sulfur 变成 sulfide：zinc sulfide。

whyWrong.en: "Heated" is what we did, not a substance. The name must start with the metal: zinc.
whyWrong.zh: heated 是我们做的动作，不是物质。名字要以金属开头：zinc。

items.q: Name TWO compounds from: calcium carbonate, iron, sulfur, carbon dioxide, chlorine.

why.en: Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) both have different atoms joined. Iron, sulfur and chlorine are elements.
why.zh: 碳酸钙 (CaCO₃) 和二氧化碳 (CO₂) 都是不同原子结合。铁、硫、氯是元素。

whyWrong.en: Carbon dioxide is right! The question asks for TWO, and iron sulfide was not in the list. The second one is calcium carbonate.
whyWrong.zh: 二氧化碳是对的！题目要两个，而且硫化铁不在列表里。第二个是碳酸钙。

items.q: Is iron sulfide the same as the iron and sulfur mixture? Explain using a magnet.
items.right: No. A magnet pulls iron out of the mixture, but not out of iron sulfide, because the iron is joined to sulfur in a new substance.

why.en: Mixture = not joined, so the magnet separates them. Compound = joined, so the magnet cannot.
why.zh: 混合物 = 没有结合，所以磁铁能分开；化合物 = 结合了，所以磁铁分不开。

whyWrong.en: Left empty. Use this starter: "No, because ..."
whyWrong.zh: 没有写。可以用这个开头：No, because ...

items.q: Melting chocolate: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Still chocolate, and it can set again.
why.zh: 还是巧克力，还能再凝固。

items.q: Dissolving sugar in water: physical or chemical change?

why.en: No new substance. Boil off the water and the sugar is still there.
why.zh: 没有新物质。把水煮干，糖还在。

items.q: Boiling water: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Water becomes steam and can turn back into water.
why.zh: 水变成水蒸气，还能变回水。

items.q: Cooking an egg: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Cooking makes new substances in the egg, and you cannot make it raw again.
why.zh: 煮鸡蛋生成了新物质，鸡蛋变不回生的。

whyWrong.en: It looks like a heating change, but ask: can it change back? An egg can never be uncooked.
whyWrong.zh: 看起来像加热变化，但要问：能变回去吗？鸡蛋永远变不回生的。

items.q: Rusting iron: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Iron joins with oxygen and water to make rust, a new substance.
why.zh: 铁和氧、水结合生成铁锈，是新物质。

items.q: Burning paper: physical or chemical change?

why.en: Burning makes ash and gases. You cannot get the paper back.
why.zh: 燃烧生成灰和气体，纸变不回来。

items.q: Which element is a liquid at 0 °C?

why.en: Mercury melts at -39 °C and boils at 357 °C. 0 is in between, so it is a liquid.
why.zh: 汞的熔点是 -39 °C，沸点是 357 °C。0 在中间，所以是液体。

items.q: Which element is a solid at 1500 °C?

why.en: Iron melts at 1540 °C. 1500 is colder than that, so iron is still solid.
why.zh: 铁的熔点是 1540 °C。1500 比它低，所以铁还是固体。

items.q: Which element is a gas at 2000 °C?

why.en: Magnesium boils at 1100 °C, so at 2000 °C it is a gas. Mercury is a gas too.
why.zh: 镁的沸点是 1100 °C，所以 2000 °C 时是气体。汞也是气体。

items.q: Which TWO elements are liquids at 1000 °C?

why.en: Aluminium: 660 to 2520 °C. Magnesium: 650 to 1100 °C. 1000 is inside both ranges.

whyWrong.en: Aluminium is right, but it was written twice. Check each element in the table: is 1000 between its melting and boiling points?
whyWrong.zh: 铝是对的，但写了两次。在表里检查每种元素：1000 是否在熔点和沸点之间？

items.q: Put in order, smallest first: 12, -39, 0, -100, -5

why.en: All negative numbers are smaller than 0. Further from 0 on the left = smaller.
why.zh: 所有负数都比 0 小。在数轴上离 0 越远（左边）越小。

whyWrong.en: 0 was put before -39 and -5, but 0 is BIGGER than every negative number.
whyWrong.zh: 0 放在了 -39 和 -5 前面，但 0 比所有负数都大。

why.en: Start at 3 and go down 10 steps: -7.
why.zh: 从 3 往下走 10 步：-7。

why.en: Start at -4 and go up 9 steps: 5.
why.zh: 从 -4 往上走 9 步：5。

why.en: Start at -6 and go down 4 more: -10.
why.zh: 从 -6 再往下走 4 步：-10。

why.en: Up 2 from -2 lands on 0.
why.zh: 从 -2 往上 2 步正好到 0。

items.q: The temperature goes from -5 °C to 8 °C. How many degrees did it go up?

why.en: 5 degrees up to 0, then 8 more: 13 °C.
why.zh: 先升 5 度到 0，再升 8 度：13 °C。

items.q: Mercury melts at -39 °C and boils at 357 °C. How many degrees between them?

why.en: 357 - (-39) = 357 + 39 = 396 °C. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

whyWrong.en: Left empty. The hint gives the start: 357 + 39.
whyWrong.zh: 没有写。提示已经给了开头：357 + 39。

items.q: Iron 2.0 g → iron sulfide 2.8 g. How much did the mass increase?
Why did the mass go up? Use the word sulfur.
items.right: Because 0.8 g of sulfur joined the iron.

why.en: The iron did not get heavier by itself. Sulfur atoms joined on, so the mass went up.
why.zh: 铁自己不会变重。是硫原子结合上去，所以质量增加了。

whyWrong.en: Left empty. Use the starter: "The mass increased because ..."
whyWrong.zh: 没有写。用这个开头：The mass increased because ...

items.q: 5.0 g magnesium → 8.3 g magnesium oxide. How much oxygen joined?

why.en: Oxygen from the air joined on: 8.3 - 5.0 = 3.3 g.
why.zh: 空气中的氧结合上去：8.3 - 5.0 = 3.3 克。

title.zh: 第 3 天：固体、液体和气体

message.en: Great particle drawings! Today: condensing, and nitrogen is an element.
message.zh: 粒子图画得很好！今天练习：凝结，以及氮气是元素。

missing.en: Pages 9 and 10 have not been checked yet. Please send photos of them to Roy.
missing.zh: 第 9 页和第 10 页还没有批改。请把照片发给 Roy 老师。

title.zh: 第 8 页：固体、液体和气体

items.q: Draw about 12 particles for solid, liquid and gas.
items.her: solid tight rows, liquid close but random, gas spread out
items.right: solid: neat rows; liquid: close, random; gas: far apart

why.en: Your drawings show the three states clearly.
why.zh: 你的图清楚地画出了三种状态。

items.q: solid → liquid is called?

why.en: Solid to liquid = melting.
why.zh: 固体变液体 = 熔化。

items.q: liquid → gas is called?

why.en: Liquid to gas = boiling.
why.zh: 液体变气体 = 沸腾。

items.q: liquid → solid is called?

why.en: Liquid to solid = freezing.
why.zh: 液体变固体 = 凝固。

items.q: gas → liquid is called?

why.en: Gas back to liquid = condensing (like water drops on a cold glass).
why.zh: 气体变回液体 = 凝结（像冷杯子外的水珠）。

whyWrong.en: Boiling goes the OTHER way (liquid → gas). The arrow here points from gas back to liquid.
whyWrong.zh: 沸腾方向相反（液体 → 气体）。这里箭头是从气体回到液体。

items.q: Which statement about liquids is correct?
items.her: c) no fixed shape, but a fixed volume
items.right: c) no fixed shape, but a fixed volume

why.en: A liquid takes the shape of its container but keeps its volume.
why.zh: 液体形状随容器变，但体积不变。

items.q: Particles change from regular (neat rows) to random. Which process?

why.en: Solid (neat rows) → liquid (random) = melting.
why.zh: 固体（整齐）→ 液体（无序）= 熔化。

items.q: Which TWO words apply to nitrogen?

why.en: Nitrogen (N₂) is a gas in the air, and it has only one kind of atom: element.
why.zh: 氮气 (N₂) 是空气里的气体，只有一种原子：元素。

whyWrong.en: Gas is right, but N₂ has only N atoms, so it cannot be a compound.
whyWrong.zh: 气体是对的，但 N₂ 只有 N 原子，所以不是化合物。

items.q: Which TWO words apply to copper sulfate (blue crystals, CuSO₄)?

why.en: Crystals are solid; Cu, S and O are joined: compound.
why.zh: 晶体是固体；Cu、S、O 结合：化合物。

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.right: b) There are 2 liquid elements at room temperature.

why.en: Mercury and bromine are the two liquid elements at room temperature.
why.zh: 汞和溴是室温下的两种液态元素。

whyWrong.en: Most metals are NOT magnetic. Only a few are, like iron, nickel and cobalt.
whyWrong.zh: 大部分金属没有磁性，只有少数有，比如铁、镍、钴。

message.en: Start with the lesson together, then do the activities in order.
message.zh: 先一起看课堂幻灯片，再按顺序做练习。
